items.title: 'Caught lying': Police bashed Brad, then charged him with assaulting them
items.description: After fracturing about a dozen of a man's ribs and puncturing his lung, police officers discussed how to explain what happened to him.

items.title: Why is Labor spending its political majority on this tax reform?
items.description: Why has Labor decided to spend the political capital of a 50-seat majority on a minor change to capital gains tax on businesses?

items.title: Young Australians reject budget as One Nation popularity climbs further
items.description: Labor's federal budget is falling flat with its target demographic as millennials say they would rather vote for One Nation than Labor or the Greens, according to a new Redbridge poll.

items.title: Byron Bay faces reckoning as women reveal predatory 2000s culture
items.description: Rachel Kila has waived her right to anonymity to join dozens of others speaking out about the experiences of young girls in Byron Bay in the early 2000s, where they say it became normalised for older boys and men to groom and have sex with girls then publicly humiliate them.

items.title: Australian housing market stalls in May
items.description: Australia's housing market continues to lose momentum, with national home values flatlining in May as higher interest rates, weak confidence and proposed property tax changes weigh on demand.

items.title: Quietly published Liberal Party paper raises gender membership concerns
items.description: The Liberal Party has quietly published a paper that floats offering a cut price $10 digital membership to join the party, in an effort to offset its declining numbers.

items.title: Iran weekly briefing: Trump demands changes to peace plan
items.description: Donald Trump is reported to be amending a peace plan, which could fuel further delays in finding a final agreement.

items.title: Inside the new 'ghost proxy' terror group 'we need to take seriously'
items.description: Australia would be the "perfect" target for a fledgling Islamist terror network that has carried out antisemitic attacks in Europe, the UK and Canada, experts have warned.

items.title: Australia scraps new Virginia-class submarines in AUKUS shake-up
items.description: The US, UK and Australia have announced they will "streamline" the purchase, with Australia no longer buying new submarines, and acquiring three second-hand ones.

items.title: One-third of Ian Thorpe's life was in the spotlight, and it took its toll
items.description: Ian Thorpe became a global star as a teenager, attracting both opportunities and scrutiny. Now, he wishes he'd done some things differently.

items.title: Shein, Kmart deny copying designs from Queensland retailer Sabo Skirt
items.description: Shein and Kmart have fired back at Sabo Skirt in an intellectual property dispute, claiming the designs they were accused of copying were substantially similar to pre-existing designs.

items.title: Roadside stalls are booming, with 45,000 members in one group alone
items.description: Nestled away in the Adelaide Hills are dozens of roadside stalls dedicated to local produce including baked goods and bouquets — and business is both booming and blooming.

items.title: Brazil authorities investigate two possible Ebola cases as outbreak grows
items.description: The true reach of the Ebola outbreak in central Africa could be much wider than the official figures published by central African authorities, the World Health Organization is warning.

items.title: Virgin holds $90m in unclaimed COVID flight credits. They expire in a month
items.description: The airline had more than $90 million in unspent travel credits on its books earlier this year.

items.title: When does getting a 'prenup' or a binding financial agreement make sense?
items.description: Binding financial agreements take time and money to obtain. Here's how they work.

items.title: Quiz: Will you be crowned the history champ this week?
items.description: Who took the first five-wicket haul in one-day cricket? And which state capital was the last to get ABC TV?

items.title: How Trials turned traumatic childhood into triumphant solo album
items.description: The prolific A.B. Original rapper-producer talks about learning to "marry the wrong feeling with the right music".

items.title: Melbourne Fringe board rejects artists' request for 'fair cut'
items.description: An open letter to festival organisers that attracted almost 600 signatures asked them to "give artists a fair cut", with specific requests to change the way fees are calculated.

items.title: US Navy interested in using controversial Darwin ship lift, NT minister says
items.description: Northern Territory Infrastructure Minister Bill Yan says the United States Navy has expressed interest in using the controversial Darwin ship lift, which is expected to be operational next year.

items.title: Police investigate Melbourne house fire that left one dead and another injured
items.description: A person has died in a house fire in Werribee and another person has been taken to hospital with serious injuries.

items.title: West Coast claims fourth win as Essendon's injury nightmare continues
items.description: West Coast makes light work of Essendon at Perth Stadium, as the Bombers lose another promising youngster to a serious injury.

items.title: Haas laments Broncos' BS as Maguire warns against hoping for another miracle
items.description: After four straight losses, the 5-7 Broncos are in the same position as last year before launching an audacious run to the premiership, but coach Michael Maguire says the team should not expect to be able to do that again.

items.title: Dozens killed by blast in rebel-held Myanmar village
items.description: Authorities say the blast was likely caused by explosives used for mining that had been stored in a warehouse.

items.title: Lucky escape for pair as tree falls on car amid WA wild weather
items.description: Two people have had a lucky escape after a tree fell onto their car on a major highway in WA's South West this afternoon, as strong winds lashed the region.

items.title: Horses bolt through Rome after police officer sets off fireworks
items.description: Fireworks set off without permission by a police officer during a rehearsal for Italy's Republic Day parade startled dozens of horses, sending them bolting through the capital and injuring several riders.
